transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well... I guess I've just been trying to get someone to actually take this seriously. It’s been going on for over a year now at my job. 

They started this new ticket rotation, and doing all these security audits. It's... well, they're using it to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps pulling me in and showing me the system logs, trying to tell me it’s just standard policy, but... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t?
No. ...No, nothing like that. I don't... hear voices, if that's what you mean. I just see the actual system logs they put in front of me. That's all.
Has anyone told you that your speech is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?
No. ...No, nobody's ever said that. I speak perfectly fine. I just tell them what I see, and that's it.
Do you ever feel that someone else is putting thoughts into your mind?
No. ...I don't know what you mean by that. My thoughts are my own.
Do you think it’s possible that your manager and the system logs are not actually part of a plot against you?

No. ...I don't. 

I've been trying for over a year now to get someone to actually take this seriously. Management keeps showing me those logs and... and saying it's just policy. But the new ticket rotation, the security audits... they're clearly using them to build a paper trail against me. 

That's why I'm here. I know what I'm looking at.
Do you believe your manager is targeting you because of something very unusual or impossible, like being controlled by outside forces or having special powers involved?
No. Nothing like that. Just... regular workplace retaliation. They just want me out.
Do you think your manager is acting this way because of any specific reason, or is it completely without a clear reason?

I don't know. ...I haven't given them a reason. 

They probably just... decided I've been there too long, maybe. Or they just want me gone. I don't know the exact reason why. I just see what's happening.
What evidence do you have that your manager is specifically targeting you?

I... I already said. It's the ticket rotation. And the audits. 

They say it's just policy, but... I know what I'm looking at. I've been doing this a long time. The way they assign the tickets now, the way my work is being audited... they're building a paper trail. 

That's the evidence. I've been trying to get someone to see it for a year.
Has this belief caused problems with your job performance or ability to function there?

I mean... I guess things are a little different. 

I don't really want to get involved in certain network projects anymore. And I... I make sure to document everything. I write out longer notes in my tickets now, just to protect myself. 

It takes more time. And the meetings... they aren't as smooth as they used to be. It's harder to work with the rest of the team when I'm just trying to watch my back.

No. ...I don't think so.

So... no. I don't think I'm wrong about this.
Have you had any other unusual beliefs or experiences besides the idea that your manager is targeting you?
No. Not really. I just... I go to work, I do my job, and I come home. That's all. There's nothing else going on.
Did anything specific happen at work that first made you think your manager was targeting you?
It was... about a year and two months ago. When they brought in the hybrid schedule. And they made those changes to the after-hours tickets. That's when it started.
When you think about it, is there any chance at all that the changes at work were not actually aimed at you?

I... I thought I just answered that. No. 

Like I said... I've been trying to get someone to take this seriously for over a year now. Management keeps bringing out their logs, telling me it's just standard policy for everyone. But... the ticket rotation, those security audits... it's a paper trail. They are building it against me. 

So... no. I don't see how it could be anything else.
Do you ever find that your thoughts get jumbled or hard to keep on track when you’re talking?
No. My mind is fine. I know exactly what I'm saying.
